reason: Re-opened packet.js veda 56 --verse 5.85.6 (revision 209192, pinned for 5.85). Evidence re-found verbatim: māyāṃ prajñām (magic taken as wisdom); idaṃ varuṇasya mahat karma; and the deed from spreading the mid-air to the unfilled sea must not be said to befit Parameśvara alone and not Varuṇa, tasya varuṇādirūpāvasthānāt (since He abides in the forms of Varuṇa and the rest), with eṣa brahma. So deed fitly Varuna’s, since the Supreme Lord abides in the forms of Varuna and the other gods is carried; the other gods is a fair English for ādi. Wilson’s note drops na vācyam and inverts Sāyaṇa; the entry follows the Sanskrit, not Wilson. Plain sense: day.js shows 5.85.5 and 5.85.6 declare Varuna’s deed of magic and 5.85.7 to 8 ask him to remove trespass and sins, so before the hymn turns to pleas for pardon holds. verse.js ok (5.85.6, at [438,6], 33 words); entry-check ok. Only nit: the singer marvels at the sea loosely names the object of wonder, which is the god’s deed with the sea; not false.
better: Context clause could read: “...the singer marvels at Varuna’s deed with the sea;” (check the cap and the four-word rule).
